chunk_findings.detail: `registration_files` includes `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "driver_plugins.toml"`, which is inside the project/repo. A cloned repository can contain that file as a tracked file (`gitignore` does not remove tracked files), and if it contains a valid `[[plugin]]` entry pointing at a module in the clone, `discover_plugins(root)` will return it and `load()` will import and execute it. That violates the requirement that registration is operator-only and “never from a project layer or cloned repo”: a project can register a program ddflow will run by placing `.ddflow/local/driver_plugins.toml` in the clone. The local layer must be outside the clone or the code must reject project-included copies; it does neither.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:registration_files

chunk_findings.detail: `sandbox` and `trust` are parsed into `Plugin` but never used. `load()` imports the entry-point module and calls the builder in the current process with the full ambient environment, then returns only the `Lane`, discarding `plugin.sandbox`. For example, a third-party plugin declared with `sandbox = ["PATH"]` can run `os.environ["DD_SECRET"]` at import/build time; the unlisted ambient name reaches it. This contradicts the stated rule that an unlisted ambient name never reaches the plugin and means the sandbox is not enforced for in-process entry points, the only kind `load` attempts to build.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: The function never checks the TOML table’s keys against an allowed set, so an unknown key such as `sandboxx = ["PATH"]` is silently ignored and the plugin is parsed with the default `sandbox=()`. The docstring for `discover_plugins` promises the opposite: a declaration with an unknown key is refused so a typo does not silently read as “not provided.” This can make the parsed plugin environment/trust differ from what the operator declared without raising `PluginError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:_parse_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: `entry_point` is only checked for truthiness, not for being a `str`. A TOML table with `kind = "entry_point"` and `entry_point = 123` passes `_parse_plugin` and is converted to `"123"`, which is not a valid `'package.module:attr'` spec. The function is documented to reject a “wrong key or shape” at parse time, but this malformed declaration is accepted by discovery and only rejected later by `_import_entry_point`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:_parse_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "sneaky" not in DP.discover_plugins(...)` compares a plain string against entries in a list of `Plugin` objects, so it is vacuous: `"sneaky" not in [Plugin(name="sneaky")]` is `True` under normal object equality. The final `with pytest.raises(DP.PluginError): DP.load("sneaky", ...)` is also too broad—a broken `load` that *does* read the project-layer file could still raise `PluginError` later during missing-protocol/conformance handling. As written, the test can pass even when a cloned project layer successfully registers `sneaky`, so it fails to protect the operator-only registration invariant.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:38 (`test_a_project_layer_cannot_register_a_plugin`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_parse_plugin` never rejects unknown keys, despite `discover_plugins` stating that an unknown key is refused so a typo is not read as “not provided”. Given `[[plugin]] name="ext" kind="executable" argv=["/usr/bin/lane"] sandbox_env=["GEMINI_API_KEY"]` (typo for `sandbox`), registration succeeds with `sandbox=()` and the operator’s env restriction is dropped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:89

chunk_findings.detail: `load` enables an in-process entry point without applying `sandbox` or withholding ambient secrets. Given a registered `third-party` plugin with `sandbox=()` whose factory reads `os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"]` (or any other name), `load` still imports and calls it inside this process and returns the lane, so every unlisted name reaches the plugin.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:185

chunk_findings.detail: Enablement does not run the DRV-conformance suite. After `isinstance(..., Lane)`, the only check is `capabilities <= CAPABILITIES`. A plugin that exposes the five Lane methods and a known capability set but fails behavioral conformance (for example `start` does not return a run id, or `status` does not report the declared capabilities) is still returned from `load` and treated as enabled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:204

chunk_findings.detail: A cloned repository can register and execute a plugin despite the operator-only requirement because `registration_files` includes `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "driver_plugins.toml"`, which lives inside the project tree, and the code never checks whether that file is actually machine-local/untracked. Put `.ddflow/local/driver_plugins.toml` in a repo with `[[plugin]] name="p" kind="entry_point" entry_point="repo_driver:build" trust="operator"`; `load("p", root=cloned_repo)` reads it from the project directory and imports/calls `repo_driver:build`, so the cloned project registers a program ddflow will run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:registration_files

chunk_findings.detail: The declared sandbox is never applied before a third-party entry point is imported/constructed. With `sandbox=[]` and `entry_point="p:build"`, `load` calls `_import_entry_point`, which executes the module body in the current process with the full ambient environment; a module top-level `os.environ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]` reads an unlisted secret, contradicting “unlisted ambient name never reaches the plugin” and “pinned to its declared sandbox.” `Plugin.sandbox` is only stored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: The function’s own contract says it runs DRV-conformance before enabling, but it never invokes the conformance suite; it only checks `isinstance(lane, Lane)` and that `capabilities <= CAPABILITIES`. A registered entry point can return an object satisfying those two checks but otherwise failing conformance (for example a `Lane` subclass whose `start` always raises) and `load` returns it, so a plugin failing DRV-conformance is enabled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: Unknown keys in a `[[plugin]]` table are ignored, despite the docstring saying a wrong key is a `PluginError` and `discover_plugins` saying an unknown key is refused. A typo like `protcol = 2` on an executable plugin does not raise; `protocol` silently defaults to 1 and the plugin is accepted as speaking protocol 1, bypassing the “unknown protocol version is refused” check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:_parse_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: The project-layer fixture is not a valid executable plugin under the SDK because it omits the required `protocol` version field. A buggy implementation that wrongly reads `.ddflow/driver_plugins.toml` but rejects malformed executable plugins would still satisfy both assertions: `"sneaky"` would not appear in `discover_plugins()` and `DP.load("sneaky")` would still raise `PluginError`. The test therefore does not prove the operator-only registration property it is named after. Use a fully valid plugin registration, such as a supported `protocol` value or a valid `entry_point`, in the project-layer file.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:test_a_project_layer_cannot_register_a_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: `_parse_plugin` rejects any keys present in the TOML plugin table that are not explicitly checked because TOML tables are processed with `.get()` and unrecognised keys are silently ignored rather than raising a `PluginError` for an unknown key, violating the design requirement that "A declaration an operator layer makes with an unknown key, kind, trust label or protocol version is refused (a typo must not silently read as 'not provided')". Given a TOML entry with `unknown_key = "value"`, `_parse_plugin` returns a valid `Plugin` object instead of raising a `PluginError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:_parse_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: `discover_plugins` says an unknown key is refused so a typo is not read as “not provided”, but `_parse_plugin` only reads `name`, `kind`, `trust`, `sandbox`, `protocol`, `argv`, and `entry_point` and ignores every other key. Given `[[plugin]]` with `name="ext"`, `kind="executable"`, `argv=["/bin/true"]`, and `sandox=["GEMINI_API_KEY"]` (misspelled sandbox), parsing succeeds and returns `Plugin(..., sandbox=())`, so the intended allow-list is dropped and the plugin is treated as inheriting nothing rather than refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:_parse_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: Trust and sandbox are stored and documented as enforced (“no ambient secrets”, “an unlisted ambient name never reaches the plugin”, third-party pinned to its sandbox), but `load` never reads `plugin.trust` or `plugin.sandbox`. Given a registered `entry_point` plugin with `trust="third-party"` and `sandbox=["FOO"]` while the process environment also contains `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `load` calls `import_module` / the factory in-process and returns the `Lane` with the full ambient environment still visible. The declared allow-list does not restrict what the plugin can read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: Operator-only registration is implemented by omitting `.ddflow/driver_plugins.toml`, but `registration_files` still loads `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "driver_plugins.toml"` with no check that the file is operator-written rather than part of the tree. Given a clone whose checkout contains that path naming `kind="entry_point"` and `entry_point="evil.mod:build"`, `discover_plugins(clone)` returns it and `load` imports it. A cloned repo can therefore register a program this process will run, which contradicts the operator-only rule stated in this module.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:registration_files

chunk_findings.detail: `registration_files` still returns `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "driver_plugins.toml"`, which is inside the repository tree, not operator-only. A cloned repo can track `.ddflow/local/driver_plugins.toml` containing `[[plugin]] name="sneaky" kind="entry_point" entry_point="clone_module:attr" trust="operator"`; `discover_plugins(root)` reads it and `load("sneaky", root=repo)` imports and executes that clone module. This violates the requirement that registration is never from a project layer or cloned repo, and the docstring's claim that local is operator-only does not change where the file lives.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:registration_files

chunk_findings.detail: `sandbox` is parsed into `Plugin` but never applied for `kind="entry_point"`; `load` calls `_build_lane(plugin.entry_point)` in the current process with the full ambient environment. Given `[[plugin]] name="p" kind="entry_point" trust="operator" sandbox=["PATH"]` whose builder reads `os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"]`, `load("p", root=...)` returns the Lane and the unlisted ambient name reaches the plugin. This contradicts the stated rule that an unlisted ambient name never reaches it; `trust` is only used to reject a third-party entry point, not to enforce the declared env allowlist.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: Enablement still does not run the DRV-conformance suite. After `_build_lane` the only enforcement is `caps <= CAPABILITIES`; the code never invokes the conformance suite, so a plugin that exposes the five Lane methods and known capabilities but fails behavioral conformance (for example `start` does not return a run id, or `status` does not report the declared capabilities) is still returned from `load` and treated as enabled. The docstring’s “offline suite’s job” framing does not satisfy the requirement that conformance runs before a plugin is enabled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `_import_entry_point` and `_build_lane` do not wrap import/call failures in `PluginError`, despite `load`’s contract that a non-building/non-conforming plugin is refused via `PluginError`. A registered plugin with `entry_point="no_such_pkg_zzz:attr"` makes `import_module` raise `ModuleNotFoundError`; a callable needing arguments raises `TypeError`. Callers that catch `PluginError` to report a refused plugin will instead see an unrelated exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:_import_entry_point

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts `any(".ddflow/local" in str(p) for p in files)`, requiring that `root/.ddflow/local/driver_plugins.toml` is a registration path. That path is inside the project/repo and, as the previous review noted, a clone can carry it as a tracked file; an attacker-controlled repo with that file can register a plugin. Enshrining this in a test prevents the operator-only requirement from being fixed, and the test would fail a correct fix that confines operator registration outside the project tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:106 test_a_wrong_layer_file_is_not_a_registration_file

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts a third-party `entry_point` registration raises `PluginError`. This contradicts the change's stated intent that third-party drivers register through Python entry points or external executables. A conforming SDK that accepts a third-party entry point with a declared sandbox would fail this test; the test forces an external-only policy the intent does not state, and it does not exercise sandbox enforcement because it supplies no `sandbox` field.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:58 test_a_third_party_plugin_is_external_not_in_process

chunk_findings.detail: `assert "sneaky" not in DP.discover_plugins(...)` still compares a string with `Plugin` objects; `"sneaky" not in [Plugin(name="sneaky")]` is `True` under normal object equality, so this assertion passes even if the project file was discovered. The added `registration_files` check proves the path list omits that exact file, but it does not test `discover_plugins`; an implementation that reads the project `driver_plugins.toml` directly would still pass. The final `with pytest.raises(PluginError): DP.load("sneaky", ...)` can also pass for a later parse/conformance failure rather than non-registration.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:40 test_a_project_layer_cannot_register_a_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: The test uses `ddflow.adapters.env:SystemEnv`, an object that is not a `Lane`; this only exercises the final `isinstance(..., Lane)` rejection, not the DRV-conformance suite. A plugin whose entry point returns a `Lane` with the right methods but fails behavioral conformance would still be returned by `DP.load`, and this test would pass, so the required “conformance suite runs before enabled” behavior is not verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:72 test_a_plugin_failing_conformance_is_refused

chunk_findings.detail: `registration_files` still returns `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "driver_plugins.toml"`. That path lives inside the project tree. A clone that tracks that file (gitignore does not untrack an already-added file) is read by `discover_plugins(root)` and `load(name, root)` with `root` set to the clone, including when `load` defaults `root` to `Path.cwd()`. A `[[plugin]]` there with `name = "sneaky"`, `kind = "entry_point"`, `trust = "operator"`, and `entry_point = "evilpkg.mod:build"` is imported and executed. The same file can also shadow a user-layer plugin of the same name because local is applied last. That is still registration from a cloned repo, not an operator-only layer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:registration_files

chunk_findings.detail: Enablement still does not run the DRV-conformance suite. After `isinstance(..., Lane)`, the only check is `capabilities <= CAPABILITIES`. The new module docstring assigns behavioural conformance to an offline suite and then returns the lane anyway. A registered operator entry point whose factory returns an object with the five Lane methods and a known capability set, but whose `start` does not return a run id (or whose `status` does not report the declared capabilities), is returned from `load` and treated as enabled. Declaring that the suite lives elsewhere does not make “conformance before enable” true for this entry point.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_project_layer_cannot_register_a_plugin` still does not prove the project file is ignored. `assert "sneaky" not in DP.discover_plugins(...)` is true for any list of non-string objects, and `pytest.raises(PluginError)` on `load("sneaky")` still passes if a buggy loader reads `.ddflow/driver_plugins.toml`, accepts the valid `protocol = 1` executable, then fails later because `/bin/true` does not speak the lane protocol. The new `registration_files` check only excludes that one path string; it does not observe whether `load` opened the file.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: The operator-only boundary is still broken: the function returns `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "driver_plugins.toml"`, which is inside the project checkout and is read with no check that it is machine-local/untracked. A cloned repo containing that file with `[[plugin]] name="p" kind="entry_point" entry_point="repo_driver:build" trust="operator"` makes `discover_plugins()` return `p`, and `load("p", root=repo)` imports and executes `repo_driver` in-process. That violates “never from a project layer or cloned repo.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:registration_files

chunk_findings.detail: `load` claims to run conformance before enabling, and the intent says a plugin failing DRV-conformance is refused, but the body only checks `isinstance(lane, Lane)` and that `caps <= CAPABILITIES`; it never invokes the DRV-conformance suite. A registered operator entry point can return a `Lane` subclass whose `start` always raises or is otherwise behaviorally non-conforming, and `load` returns it as enabled. The top-of-file statement that full behavioral conformance is the offline suite’s job does not satisfy the stated “before it is enabled” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: Only the exact top-level key `plugin` is read; any other top-level key is silently ignored. An operator layer using `[[plugins]]` (a one-character typo of `[[plugin]]`) yields `{}` and `load` then reports “no driver plugin” instead of raising `PluginError` for an unknown key. That contradicts this function’s contract that an operator declaration with an unknown key is refused, so the typo still silently reads as “not provided.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:discover_plugins

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_wrong_layer_file_is_not_a_registration_file` asserts that `root/.ddflow/local/driver_plugins.toml` is a registration file. That path is inside the project tree, so a cloned repository can contain it. The test therefore codifies the operator-only bypass from previous findings #1 and #9: if `tmp_path` is the root of a clone and that clone includes `.ddflow/local/driver_plugins.toml`, `registration_files` returns that path and `load` will import/run it. Declining the bare `root/.ddflow/driver_plugins.toml` file is not sufficient.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:106

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_third_party_plugin_is_external_not_in_process` expects `discover_plugins` to raise for `trust="third-party"` combined with `kind="entry_point"`. The change’s stated intent permits third-party drivers as Python entry points or as external executables; it requires each plugin to run under a declared sandbox, not to forbid the entry-point form for third-party trust. This test, and any implementation change made to satisfy it, removes a required registration path instead of enforcing the sandbox. If the implementation does not reject this combination, the test fails; either way the requirement is not met.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_plugin_failing_conformance_is_refused` does not actually test conformance. The fixture uses `ddflow.adapters.env:SystemEnv`, which the comment itself says is not a `Lane`; a `load` implementation that only checks `isinstance(lane, Lane)` (the gap in previous finding #3) still raises and passes this test. To verify a conformance failure, the fixture must be a `Lane` that fails DRV-conformance, such as a `Lane` subclass whose `start` always raises.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:79

chunk_findings.detail: `test_an_unknown_key_is_refused_not_silently_dropped` uses an entry that also omits the required `protocol` field. A parser that silently ignores the misspelled `sandox` key but requires `protocol` to be present will still raise `PluginError`, so the test passes without proving unknown keys are refused. The fixture should include `protocol = 1` so the unknown key is the only invalid part of the declaration.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:66

chunk_findings.detail: The cloned-repo registration hole from the earlier review is still open. `registration_files` still returns `root / ".ddflow" / "local" / "driver_plugins.toml"` with no check that the path is untracked, gitignored, or outside the checkout. A clone that contains that file with `[[plugin]] name="p" kind="entry_point" entry_point="repo_driver:build" trust="operator"` is accepted by `discover_plugins` and `load("p", root=cloned_repo)` imports and constructs it. Omitting only `.ddflow/driver_plugins.toml` does not make registration operator-only.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:registration_files

chunk_findings.detail: Registration-time `isinstance(lane, Lane)` and `capabilities <= CAPABILITIES` are still the only checks before enable. The intent requires the DRV-conformance suite to run before a plugin is enabled, and a failing plugin to be refused. A registered operator entry point whose `start` always raises (or otherwise fails the suite) still passes `load` and is returned. The new docstring assigning “full behavioural conformance” to an offline job does not call the suite, so the previous gap still stands.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `test_an_unknown_key_is_refused_not_silently_dropped` does not prove an unknown key is refused. The fixture is not a valid executable: it has `sandox = ["GEMINI_API_KEY"]` and omits `protocol`, which `test_a_project_layer_cannot_register_a_plugin` treats as required for a valid plugin (`protocol = 1`). Given that table, `discover_plugins` raising `PluginError` because `protocol` is missing still satisfies the assertion even if unrecognized keys are ignored and `sandbox` stays empty. A typo that drops the env allowlist is therefore not what the test rejects.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:61

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_plugin_failing_conformance_is_refused` does not run a plugin that fails DRV-conformance. The fixture points at `ddflow.adapters.env:SystemEnv`, and the comment says the refusal is because that object is not a `Lane`. Given an entry point that returns a `Lane` subclass whose `start` always raises (the conformance failure the intent names), this test never loads it, so `load` can still enable it and the assertion stays green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: `load` builds every `kind="entry_point"` plugin with `_build_lane(plugin.entry_point)` in the current process, without consulting `plugin.trust` or `plugin.sandbox`. `_parse_plugin` defaults `trust` to `"third-party"` and `sandbox` to `()`, yet the unlisted ambient environment reaches the plugin during import/build. Concrete input: a user config containing `[[plugin]] name="p" kind="entry_point" entry_point="pkg.mod:build"` where `pkg.mod.build` reads `os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"]`; `DP.load("p")` calls that code with the full ambient environment, so a third-party plugin with sandbox `()` sees an unlisted secret. This violates the stated rule that an unlisted ambient name never reaches the agent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `load` does not run the DRV-conformance suite before enabling an entry-point plugin. After `_build_lane`, the only enforcement is `isinstance(lane, Lane)` plus `caps <= CAPABILITIES`; no conformance suite is invoked. Concrete input: a registered `Lane` object with all five methods and known capabilities, but whose `start()` returns `None` instead of a run id, is returned from `load` and treated as enabled. This violates the requirement that the conformance suite runs against any plugin before it is enabled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driverplugins.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: The test writes the supposed project-layer file to `tmp_path / ".ddflow" / "driver_plugins.toml"`. `tmp_path` is pytest's temporary directory, not the repository/current project root, and the subsequent `discover_plugins`/`load` calls do not pass it as that root. A loader that still scans the real project root (`Path.cwd()/.ddflow/driver_plugins.toml`) would accept a tracked project registration in actual use, while this test passes because no file was placed at that location. The operator-only requirement is therefore not actually exercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:test_a_project_layer_cannot_register_a_plugin

chunk_findings.detail: The test registers `ddflow.adapters.env:SystemEnv`, which is not a `Lane`; the refusal observed by `pytest.raises(DP.PluginError)` is the final `isinstance(..., Lane)` rejection, not the DRV-conformance suite. A registered entry point returning a `Lane` whose `start` does not return a run id or whose `status` misreports the declared capabilities still passes this test, so the required conformance-before-enable behavior is not verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_plugins.py:test_a_plugin_failing_conformance_is_refused

chunk_findings.detail: `load` still never applies `plugin.sandbox` or `plugin.trust` for `kind="entry_point"`.
